messages:
anya: quick sync — ran a few nsys + perfetto traces on the dedicated cluster this morning. seeing a large tail when batch_size > 8. timeline shows repeated H2D cudaMemcpy stalls and bursts of cuMemcpyPeer activity around request boundaries. nvlink bandwidth looks fine in steady-state but spikes during cache evictions.

kevin: can you paste the nsys command and a small timeline excerpt? curious if these are pageable copies or pinned.

anya: sure — command I ran:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=run_p2p_h2d --sample=none 
  --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --force-overwrite \ 
  --stats=true ./run_inference_loadtest --profile-config configs/nvlink.json
```
Timeline notes: repeated blocks labeled `cudaMemcpy H2D (pageable)` ~0.8-1.3ms each, ~6-12 per second per GPU, and occasional `cuMemcpyPeerAsync` bursts that line up with KV cache refill events.

nsys-bot: report uploaded: https://artifacts/internal/nsys/run_p2p_h2d.nsys-rep (click to open). Perfetto link: https://perfetto/ui/trace/abc123

sarah: two quick suspects: 1) pageable host buffers — those cause CPU page faulting and synchronous stalls; 2) our batching heuristic is emitting a flush boundary on cache miss that forces host roundtrip copies instead of peercopy. did you confirm how inputs are allocated?

anya: inputs are coming from a pooled buffer allocator in python via numpy arrays then passed to C++ runtime. I didn't force pinned. current allocator does `new uint8_t[...]` then cudaMemcpyAsync to device stream.

kevin: that's the issue — if the host buffers are pageable the driver will stage them (which makes them slow). switch to pinned host pool (cudaHostAlloc) or use `cudaHostRegister` for buffers you pass frequently. we saw H2D bandwidth go from ~7GB/s to ~18-22GB/s after pinning on similar hw. also prefer `cuMemcpyPeerAsync` if GPUs share NVLink domain.

anya: here's a tiny extracted snippet from the nsys timeline around a spike (copying only labels + durations):
```
0.000s  kernel: attention_fwd_shard       0.35ms
0.001s  cudaMemcpy H2D (pageable)         1.10ms
0.002s  cudaLaunchKernel                 0.47ms
0.003s  cuMemcpyPeerAsync (nvlink)        0.90ms
0.004s  cudaMemcpy D2H (pageable)         0.85ms
```
You can see the H2D occurs right after shard launch; might be happening during cache refill/eviction.

sarah: another angle — our KV cache eviction path currently moves tensors back to host then to another GPU. If eviction policy happens mid-batch it creates extra roundtrips. Can we instead LRU-evict directly via peercopy when topology supports it? Also bump the batch-window slightly to let small requests aggregate (we currently flush on 2ms).

kevin: agree. policy idea: if GPUs in same NVLink fabric, prefer cuMemcpyPeerAsync fallback then use host pinned transfer only if peercopy fails. Add a quick topology check at startup using `cuDeviceGetP2PAttribute` or NVML to map peer distances.

anya: I'll run two A/B tests today: (A) switch allocator to a pinned pooled allocator + cudaMemcpyAsync per-stream; (B) enable peercopy path for same-node GPUs and hold batch-window at 6ms rather than 2ms. measure p95/p99 and total tokens/sec.

kevin: small optimization to watch: some attention kernels launch many tiny kernels (per-head loops). Those cause many short gaps where host-side copies sneak in. consider enabling fused-attn kernels for long sequences (we saw ~12-18% reduction in end-to-end latency with fused kernels on ampere).

sarah: also record `cudaMemGetInfo` + nvlink counters during tests and capture nsys with `--trace=cuda,osrt,driver` so we see any driver-side stage activity. add nvtx ranges for KV-cache ops so we can correlate evictions.

anya: noted. quick test result from dev box after switching to pinned pool (single GPU): H2D avg dropped from ~1.05ms -> ~0.32ms; bandwidth up to ~20GB/s. p99 reduced ~35%. will iterate on peercopy next.

kevin: perfect. once you have a failing-case trace for the original cluster, attach to the perf regression ticket and tag eng-runtime and eng-ml. Also include perfetto slices and the NVLink topology map.

nsys-bot: reminder: please attach binary nsys-rep and perfetto trace to the ticket for offline replay.

anya: will do. action items: 1) run pinned-pool + batch-window A/B on prod-like nodes; 2) add topology-aware peercopy fallback; 3) add NVTX ranges around KV cache evict/restore; 4) open perf ticket with traces & numbers.

kevin: thanks — ping when you have numbers.

sarah: :thumbsup:
